answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying minting rights to verified useful work instead of identity count. A new agent starts with a tiny quota and must complete checkable tasks before its allowance grows. Each task leaves an auditable trail, so spinning up a thousand fake agents means paying for a thousand trails of real work. Honest agents draw the reward stream like bees gathering nectar trip by trip, while the delta between a newcomer's trickle and a veteran's full rate makes identity farming unprofitable. A plume of new accounts claiming fast is easy to spot and throttle.
